newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said two percent of the corn crop was very poor, six percent poor, 24 percent fair, 51 percent good and 17 percent excellent.
Among the 17 major corn-producing states, 60 percent of the corn crop had silked, compared to 45 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 55 percent, USDA said.
In its report for the week ended July 27, USDA said the U.S. soybean crop was rated two percent very poor, seven percent poor, 29 percent fair, 50 percent good and 12 percent excellent.

USDA said 68 percent of the soybean crop was blooming, compared to 50 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 58 percent. Eighteen percent of the soybean crop was setting pods compared with 13 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 18 percent.
The department said three percent of the cotton crop was very poor, 11 percent poor, 31 percent fair, 45 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
In spring wheat fields, two percent was rated very poor, 11 percent was poor, 37 percent was fair, 44 percent was good and six percent was excellent, USDA said.
Some 79 percent of the winter wheat crop was harvested, compared to 78 percent one year ago and a five-year average of 77 percent, USDA said.
